events.finding: The main counter run has no hob, cooktop or oven — a kitchen without its cooking anchor. The long worktop is empty and the wall above is bare, so the room does not function as a kitchen.

The sink unit is a separate, taller box with a different counter height and a bare blue-grey basin that does not match the white run on the left. The two pieces read as mismatched placeholders, not one coordinated kitchen.
The 'wall cabinet' is rendered as a thin floating shelf with no doors or body, leaving the wall above the worktop empty. It does not read as storage and leaves the main run visually unfinished.
The sink bowl is a flat, untextured blue-grey slab that clashes with the white cabinetry and grey stone counters. It looks like a placeholder, not a real basin.
The entire run is a parametric box: flat white fronts, no handles, no appliance cut-outs, no backsplash. It reads as a grey-box model rather than a styled kitchen.

The main kitchen run is just a base cabinet with an empty worktop: no hob, no sink, no tap and no upper cabinets above it. A kitchen without its core appliances and storage is the single biggest reason this render fails.
The only sink is on a separate counter at the right edge, disconnected from the main run, so the primary work zone has no sink or tap and the layout does not read as a coherent kitchen.
The wall_cabinet pieces are not visible above the main run, leaving a large empty wall and reinforcing the impression of an unfinished, incomplete kitchen.
The right-hand counter with the sink is a different, lower unit that does not visually connect to the main run, making the set look mismatched rather than one designed kitchen.
Flat, untextured plaster walls and a completely bare worktop make the space look like a grey-box placeholder rather than a styled, client-ready kitchen.

The bathtub is also completely bare. There is no shower head, no faucet, no bath mat, and no caddy. It looks like an empty white box.
The toilet is missing a seat cover and any kind of decor (like a small plant or a roll of spare toilet paper), which makes the room feel sterile and incomplete.
The view through the windows is a crude, low-poly 'lollipop' landscape (blobby trees, flat green ground). This is a placeholder asset that makes the entire render look unfinished and unprofessional.
